what: Spoken-language identification: top-1 accuracy and speed of each runnable lid model on the repository's own audio (11 clips: the three bolo samples, the console's diarization and cloning samples and its two recorded mock clips; English and Hindi) and on 39 synthesised clips in 13 Indian languages (3 sentences each)
hardware: 4 vCPU x86_64 (Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz), no GPU, shared (load average 14-18 during the runs)
indian_clips: There are no recorded Indian-language test clips in the repository beyond Hindi, so 39 were synthesised with bolo's own Indian voices, one voice per language, three sentences each (everyday sentences written for this test, 2.4 to 6.9 s): hi piper-hi-in-rohan-medium, bn piper-bn-bd-google-medium, ta piper-ta-in-rasa-female-medium, te piper-te-in-padmavathi-medium, mr piper-mr-in-google-medium, gu mimic3-gu-cmu-indic, kn syspin-kn-female, ml piper-ml-in-meera-medium, pa mms-tts-pan, ur piper-ur-pk-aegis-female-medium, ne piper-ne-np-chitwan-medium, or mms-tts-ory, as mms-tts-asm. Synthetic speech from one voice per language is cleaner and more uniform than real recordings: read these numbers as a check that each model tells the languages apart, not as their accuracy on real speech.
method: a script using bolo's core (Bolo.identify_language): each model pulled from the catalog, warmed up on one clip, then core.identify_language on every clip; correct when the most likely language equals the clip's language. rtf = wall time / seconds the model heard (at most 30 s). Odia is not among the languages of Whisper, VoxLingua107 or AmberNet, so those models cannot get it right; Urdu and Hindi are one spoken language in most everyday speech, and the Urdu voice was heard as Hindi by every model

not_run.mms-lid-126: 978 MB int8 graph, over this project's 500 MB limit for measured runs on the shared test machine
not_run.voxlect-indic-lid-whisper-small: not runnable (PyTorch class from the Voxlect repository)
